conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is supported by evidence, citing a randomized clinical trial and current guidelines showing that tenofovir started in the third trimester reduces mother-to-child transmission.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
The claim is **supported by evidence**; it is not false.

A landmark randomized clinical trial (Pan et al., 2016) published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* enrolled 200 HBeAg-positive pregnant women with HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL. Daily tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) begun in the third trimester reduced mother-to-child transmission from 18% (placebo) to 5% at the primary endpoint, with no significant difference in adverse events between groups. An NYU Langone summary of the same trial reported the reduction from 18% to 5%.

Current guidelines reinforce this. The 2025 AASLD/IDSA chronic hepatitis B guideline recommends initiating TDF or tenofovir alafenamide at gestational week 28 for pregnant persons with HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL to prevent mother-to-child transmission, regardless of HBeAg status. Additional studies and reviews confirm that tenofovir significantly lowers vertical transmission and viral load and is safe and tolerable for mothers and infants.

In short, randomized trial data and current specialist guidelines both support third-trimester tenofovir for pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B and high viral load to reduce mother-to-child transmission.

Sources:

- https://nyulangone.org/news/antiviral-treatment-during-pregnancy-reduces-mother-child-transmission-hepatitis-b
- https://www.guidelinecentral.com/guideline/10618/
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30071845/
